Harness Map

How a ticket moves through the Claude Code harness, who does the work at each step, and which rules the host enforces. Generated from the harness files; CI fails when it is out of date.

7pipeline7personas9guards45conventions8session setup19skills22references36self-tests115decisions

Pipeline

Commands run in this order, and a stage can send the ticket back. Personas never start other personas. The rows with a diamond are decisions only you make.

you decideexecutor can change filescode-reviewer read-only
  1. Jira intakeFetch requirements and relevant context, surface and record blockers, and hand off to /spec without invoking itLeaves docs/specs/[TICKET]-intake.mdthe session itself
  2. /specStart spec-driven development — write a structured specification before writing codeLeaves docs/specs/[TICKET]-SPEC.md, Status: Draftrepo-recon
  3. You decide: approve spec
  4. /planBreak approved requirements into ordered, verifiable implementation tasksLeaves docs/tasks/[TICKET]-plan.md + -todo.mdSends back: /spec (SPEC CONFLICT)the session itself
  5. You decide: approve plan
  6. /buildDispatch implementation for one or more planned tasks by workstreamLeaves local commits, task Status: DoneSends back: /spec (SPEC CONFLICT) · /plan (plan defect)executor
  7. /testIndependently verify built work by running it like an engineer, for every production change skipped only for docs, test-only, formatting and generated changesLeaves VERIFY PASS / FAIL / BLOCKEDSends back: /build (VERIFY FAIL: fix the code) · /spec (the spec does not settle it)test-engineer
  8. /reviewConduct independent review and decide whether a separate VERIFY gate is requiredLeaves findings: BLOCKER / REQUIRED / ADVISORYSends back: /build (BLOCKER / REQUIRED: fix, 3 rounds max)blind-reviewercode-reviewerdistributed-systems-reviewersecurity-auditor
  9. /shipFinal release gate — synthesize review evidence into a GO/NO-GO decision with rollbackLeaves GO / NO-GO with a rollback planSends back: /build (NO-GO: fix, then /test and /review) · /spec (withdraw a requirement)the session itself
  10. You decide: push / merge
Jira intake→/spec→/plan→/build→/test→/review→/ship
Goes back
  • /plan → /spec SPEC CONFLICT
  • /build → /spec SPEC CONFLICT
  • /build → /plan plan defect
  • /test → /build VERIFY FAIL: fix the code
  • /test → /spec the spec does not settle it
  • /review → /build BLOCKER / REQUIRED: fix, 3 rounds max
  • /ship → /build NO-GO: fix, then /test and /review
  • /ship → /spec withdraw a requirement

After three review rounds /review stops, and you rethink the approach (ADR 0089).

Session setup

What every session loads: the rules in AGENTS.md and the pins in settings.json.

AGENTS.md rules
  1. Think Before CodingDon't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.Catches: confidently building the wrong thing.
  2. Simplicity FirstMinimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.Catches: a 200-line solution to a 20-line problem.
  3. Surgical ChangesTouch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.Catches: unrelated diffs that make review impossible.
  4. Goal-Driven ExecutionDefine success criteria. Loop until verified.Catches: declaring success without running anything.
  5. Deterministic Before ProbabilisticCatches: paying latency and nondeterminism for work if/else would do.
  6. Surface Conflicts, Don't Average ThemCatches: inventing a novel pattern nobody chose.
  7. Fail LoudCatches: silent gaps the reader assumes were covered.
  8. Modules Communicate Through ContractsNever reach across a module boundary. Consume the published interface.Catches: hidden coupling that turns every change into a cross-module break.
